correctness.rationale: The central square-zero ideal t=(1+z) and four-coordinate complement give complete coefficient equations. In the dihedral case A^2=0 precisely on two affine five-spaces with central four-space intersection; their distinct reflection generators have nonzero commutator. All within-branch commutators vanish and cross-branch noncentral commutators do not. Quaternion conditions force all square-zero elements into the central four-space; the three abelian cases are trivially commuting and their Frobenius coefficient counts are explicit. The adjoint map of any noncentral dihedral square-zero element has rank two, giving orbit size q^2. Direct independent multiplication tables pass exhaustive F2/F4 one-element cases and F2 pairwise and conjugacy counts; finite cases support but do not replace the symbolic proof.

Creedon--Gildea proves unit-group structure, not this induced square-zero graph.

value.rationale: The induced commuting relation on a distinguished nilpotent locus is a natural pairwise finite-algebra invariant that element counts and left regular rank alone do not determine. The classification covers all five order-eight groups and every characteristic-two finite field, and detects the smallest dihedral/quaternion contrast: one has two intersecting maximal commuting affine families whereas the other has only central square-zero elements. It also determines graph clique structure, entire pair census and the complete square-zero conjugacy orbit sizes in the nonabelian noncentral case. The restricted order eight scope is a consciously complete classification, not a single arbitrary numerical slice.
